articles.summary: The Short Version Cash-receipt document reference numbers are case sensitive. One capitalization mismatch with your org, and the whole import fails. Import lookups treat “00412” and “412” as two different customers. Spreadsheet saves strip leading zeros, and copy-paste drags in invisible trailing spaces. An invoice paid in installments can land unmatched, or hit an already-closed invoice, when your file and your ledger apply payments at different levels. Re-importing a corrected cash-receipt file creates a separate new transaction. The original record stays behind for you to clean up. Why AR CSV Integration Errors Break Cash Application In short: catch the mismatch before you click Import. Most preventable AR CSV integration failures start as a gap between your file and the import template, and untangling a half-failed batch afterward costs far more than checking the file first. My advice is simple. Treat every upload like a payment run that can’t be recalled.
articles.title: Fixing AR CSV Integration Errors: 7 Mismatch Checks Before Cash Application Breaks

articles.summary: The Short Version Credit notes and credit memos are one document with two regional labels. “Credit note” dominates across the UK and EMEA. A refund is a different animal: it sends cash back through a separate payment transaction, while a credit changes the customer’s balance and leaves the original invoice intact. Reconciliation isn’t done when the credit is created. It’s done when the credit is matched to the receivable it corrects. Issuing credits barely moves DSO, because receivables and net credit sales drop together; the aging report shows the real effect. Automatic application depends on capturing the invoice reference and reason at creation. And posted invoices, including subscription invoices already sent, need a separate credit document rather than an edit.
articles.title: Credit Note vs Credit Memo: Which One Fixes Reconciliation Faster
